text: ROOT-CAUSE analysis (worker-7, full reconciliation attempt this round): the ccp16 sf expectation cannot be fixed by the generator alone — there is a cross-impl DESIGN DIVERGENCE in step-3 gating. (1) Python ccp.py adaptive_sf_select applies steps 3-5 UNCONDITIONALLY: with threshold 8 (18jr), density 9/10 -> step-3 fires -> sf 12. (2) Rust RfHealthMetrics::adaptive_sf_select gates steps 3-4 on 'explicit' (any Some() arg): adaptive_sf_select(None,None,None) SKIPS step-3 entirely -> sf 11 (table base only). Rust's ccp_vectors_match test asserts BOTH adaptive_sf() AND adaptive_sf_select(None,None,None) equal the vector sf — impossible for density 9/10 vectors once the threshold is 8 and Python generates sf=12 (11 satisfies Rust, 12 satisfies Python). Options for Mark: (A) Rust drops the explicit gate for step-3 (steps apply unconditionally like Python; adaptive_sf_select(None) = table base + full pseudocode) then generator models full pseudocode unconditionally; (B) Python adopts explicit gating (vectors keep sf=11 for the select path; the unconditional step-3 result moves to a separate vector family); (C) vectors split into two sf fields (table_sf vs select_sf) with both impls asserting their own. Worker-7 recommends (A) — the spec pseudocode has no explicit-mode qualifier, and Rust's gating silently makes density irrelevant for the None path. The 18jr one-line threshold fix is verified correct (probe via PYTHONPATH=python/src: density 9/10 -> 12 with the fix) and should land together with whichever option is chosen + the generator update. Working tree left clean (reverted); both beads released for this decision.
